```suggestion
		jfieldID field = nullptr;
```

We don't do this for any other JNI handle types here, so I could understand saving this for a follow-up PR, but I think we probably should?
This is assuming that all field values are `Object`s. What about fields that use primitive types like bool, int, float, etc?
The method supports all types by returning `Object` as is, and autoboxing primitive types. See https://developer.android.com/reference/java/lang/reflect/Field#get(java.lang.Object) for reference.

Similar comment as above; fields with `Object` types are set as is, while values for fields with primitive types  are unboxed.
See https://developer.android.com/reference/java/lang/reflect/Field#set(java.lang.Object,%20java.lang.Object) for reference.

Are you sure this is equivalent to calling `java.lang.reflect.Field.get()`?

JNI provides different functions for each possible field type:

- `GetStaticBooleanField()`
- `GetStaticIntField()`
- etc

I don't think `GetStaticObjectField()` does autoboxing like the reflection API. But the best way to see would be to test getting a field with a primitive value and seeing what happens :-)

hmm, you may be right. I thought I tested those behaviors but I may have been testing a different code path.
I'll double-check and update if necessary.

It looks like constants are calling `java.lang.reflect.Field.get()` and then caching the result - that could be the code path you tested? Since we're already using that for the constant values, we may as well use it for the non-constant ones too?
